newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone to review gene-soybeans case by case.
newsitem.headline: Danone to review gene-soybeans case by case.

text.p: French food group Danone said on Thursday that as a consummer driven company it would decide on the use of soy products derived from genetically modified U.S. beans on a country-by-country basis.
"We are being pragmatic. We are looking at the issue on a case by case, country by country basis, and will eventually adapt," a Danone spokeswoman told Reuters.
"If in a certain country that technology becomes a problem, we may seek to diversify our supply sources or change formulas," she said.
She said that in Germany Danone had already started to diversify supply sources and formulas but did not provide further details.
Nestle France said earlier it would use products derived from gene-altered U.S. soybeans when the new 1996/97 harvest comes in.
A campaign by environmental group Greenpeace has led to concern among food processors in Germany.
The German offices of Nestle and Unilever have said they will not use the products to avoid immediate consummer opposition.

Campaigners say a possible risk to human health cannot be ruled out from the beans that have been genetically modified to resist a week killer in a technology developed by U.S. chemical company Monsanto.
